name: gdc-tcga-gbm
description:
TCGA glioblastoma is the cohort on which most glioma computational biology was built, and 1,753 articles reference it in methods or results. Its imaging is its least-used asset: radiology exists for 607 of 617 cases and histopathology for 389, held in the Imaging Data Commons rather than the GDC, which is why most analyses treat it as a molecular-only cohort.
Its follow-up is the fact most likely to trip up a new user. Median recorded follow-up is 12.0 months across 596 of 617 cases, reaching 127 months at the maximum - shorter than many users expect, because it reflects last recorded contact rather than total observation.
citeAs: Comprehensive genomic characterization defines human glioblastoma genes and core pathways

supportedQuestions: Do imaging features add prognostic or subtype information beyond molecular data in glioblastoma?
Does a new glioma classifier reproduce established methylation subgroups?
Which molecular features associate with survival in glioblastoma?

blockingLimitations.statement: Progression or recurrence is populated for 0.6% of cases and informative for none, so progression-free survival cannot be derived at all.

inappropriateUses: Claiming a classifier generalizes from TCGA-GBM performance alone.
